**Session note:** this folder isn't a git repo and has no NOTES.md, so I couldn't pull or read open items. Nothing in the repo changed, so there's no NOTES entry or push.

**Shot plan from film-crew**
- **Director:** a lifetime of craft in one quiet moment. His hands know the work while the town outside goes dark. The tone is dignity, not nostalgia.
- **Set:** black tufa stone walls (Gyumri's typical building stone), an arched west window, a walnut workbench, chisels and gouges on the wall, curled shavings on the floor, and a half-carved walnut panel with Armenian interlace ornament.
- **Costume:** a man in his 70s with white stubble, a flat cap, a grey wool vest over a faded linen shirt and a worn leather apron.
- **Camera and light:** a 35mm lens at eye level. One hard amber sunset beam is the only key light, against cool blue-grey shadow. Light haze and soft grain.
- **Camera move:** starts on his left profile, then circles 90° clockwise at a steady speed, passing through the beam halfway. It ends three-quarter front, with his face lit and his eyes on the wood.
- **Sound:** mallet taps, shavings falling, distant street sounds from the town, no music and no dialogue.

**Assumptions:** text-to-video with no references, and the master is standing at the bench. If you want his face to stay the same across several clips, make a start-frame still first (banana-pro-director-2.0) and run Kling in image-to-video mode.

## FINAL

**Video prompt — Kling 3.0, 8 s, 16:9**

**Settings:** Kling 3.0 · Text-to-Video (or Image-to-Video if you made a start-frame still) · 16:9 · 8 s · Professional / 1080p · native audio ON if your plan includes it (otherwise add the sound in post using the last line of the prompt) · leave CFG/creativity at the default · paste the negative prompt below into the Negative field.

```
Dusk inside an old stone woodcarving workshop in Gyumri, Armenia. Quiet, dignified, a lifetime of craft held in one moment.

Opening frame: medium shot at eye level, 35mm lens. An old master woodcarver stands in left profile at frame center-right behind a heavy walnut workbench that fills the lower third. Frame right, an arched window throws a single hard beam of low amber sunset light diagonally across the room. Behind him, black tufa stone walls and a rack of chisels and gouges fall into cool blue-grey shadow; pale curls of wood shavings cover the floor.

The master: a man in his seventies, white stubble, deeply lined weathered face, grey flat cap, grey wool vest over a faded linen shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbow, worn brown leather apron, fine sawdust on his forearms. A wooden mallet in his right hand, a gouge in his left, carving a half-finished walnut panel of Armenian interlace ornament. His eyes stay on the wood the whole time; he never looks at the camera.

Action: small steady mallet taps drive the gouge; a curl of shaving lifts and drops to the floor. Fine sawdust drifts slowly, glittering inside the light beam.

Camera: one slow, constant-speed orbit clockwise around him, about 90 degrees across the full 8 seconds, at eye level, smooth and weighted like a dolly on a curved track. No zoom, no cuts. Halfway through, the light beam passes between the lens and him, sawdust glowing in the foreground.

Final frame: three-quarter front medium close-up, the amber beam now across his face and hands, eyes lowered to the carving, the carved panel sharp in the lower foreground, warm window glow behind his shoulder.

Same man, same clothes, same workshop, same light direction from first frame to last; face and hands stable with natural anatomy.

Look: single warm low-angle key from the window, deep amber against cool blue-grey shadow, light haze, shallow depth of field, soft 35mm film grain, gentle low-contrast warm grade, real-time natural motion.

Sound: crisp wooden mallet taps on a steel gouge, soft wood crackle, shavings falling, distant evening street murmur, one faint far-off dog bark. No music, no speech.
```

**Negative prompt:**
```
blurry, face morphing, identity change, warped hands, extra fingers, flicker, camera shake, fast motion, cuts, zoom, text, watermark, logo, modern power tools, electric lights, music, speech
```

**Things to check after generating**
- **Camera:** the orbit should stay at a steady speed and end three-quarter front. If it spins too far, change "about 90 degrees" to "a quarter turn".
- **Face:** his face should not change while the camera crosses the beam.
- **Ornament:** the interlace pattern on the panel may come out generic. If it matters, make a start or end frame with banana-pro.
- **Rights:** no real person and no brand appear, so there's nothing to clear.
